rows.locus: cli.py `_run` function-eval branch: payload keys, status 0/6, ledger-free dispatch
rows.finding: The function-eval branch canonicalizes input and evaluates a bundle before db/partition gates, emits four keys, and returns 0/6 by matched.
rows.bearing: Root resolve can reuse the four-key result projection, but it must query ledger state and therefore cannot copy eval’s ledger-free dispatch.

rows.locus: cli.py `_run` function-verify branch: projection that keeps FunctionDocument off stdout
rows.finding: The verify branch projects passed, entries, function_hash, and ordered checks; its nested FunctionDocument never reaches stdout.
rows.bearing: Resolve must explicitly project FunctionResolution fields and nested match/check values instead of serializing the embedded document wholesale.

rows.locus: cli.py `_run` function-inspect branch: manifest projection and dropped `text`/`document`
rows.finding: The inspect branch emits operation_revision, function_hash, entries, and skipped while deliberately dropping manifest text and document fields.
rows.bearing: Resolve needs an equally explicit projection boundary so implementation-only function-document bytes remain outside its public JSON contract.

rows.locus: cli.py `main`: ordered except clauses, exception class -> exit code, stream per class
rows.finding: main maps usage/validation to 2, not-found to 3, conflict to 4, integrity to 5, and _Unverified to 6; every exception payload uses stderr.
rows.bearing: Resolve miss and verification-negative payloads required on stdout at 6 must return _Outcome rather than raise _Unverified or another mapped exception.

rows.locus: cli.py `_Outcome`: exactly-one-channel invariant and exact-int status assertion
rows.finding: _Outcome enforces exactly one of JSON payload or raw text and separately requires status to have exact type int rather than bool or a subclass.
rows.bearing: Both new leaves should use one JSON _Outcome channel for status 0/6; this invariant rejects absent, dual-channel, and non-exact statuses.

rows.locus: cli.py `_emit`: asdict expansion, sort_keys, indent, ensure_ascii, trailing newline
rows.finding: _emit expands dataclass instances with asdict, then writes ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2 JSON plus one trailing newline.
rows.bearing: The new leaves inherit byte-stable pretty JSON and dataclass expansion only after their explicit projections choose the public field set.

rows.locus: cli.py `_input`: stdin bound, buffer-vs-text branch, its three exact messages
rows.finding: _input parses inline text directly; - reads at most DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES+1 from binary or text stdin and distinguishes read, size, and UTF-8 failures.
rows.bearing: Any submit stdin channel reusing _input inherits one-value bounds and its three error families; aggregate envelopes beyond that bound need a different reader.

rows.locus: cli.py `challenge` leaf: the shipped precedent for two JSON-bearing flags on one leaf
rows.finding: The challenge leaf ships two required JSON flags, --input and --expected, and dispatch parses each independently through _input before the library call.
rows.bearing: Argparse already supports multiple JSON-bearing options on one leaf; proposal submit can expose distinct input/output channels without inventing parser machinery.

rows.locus: system.py `System.resolve`: exact signature, argument validation order, raised classes
rows.finding: resolve takes partition, operation, input_value and optional expected_function_hash; it validates names, digest, then input before ledger verification. Invalid values raise ValidationError, absent operations NotFoundError, and corrupt state IntegrityError; failed verification is a value with match=None.
rows.bearing: CLI ordering must preserve pre-ledger validation and map 2/3/5 through main, while verification-negative and ordinary-miss values require separate stdout status-6 projections.

rows.locus: system.py `System.submit_proposal`: exact signature, return type, absent revision arg
rows.finding: submit_proposal(partition, operation, input_value, *, candidate) returns str, has no revision argument, canonicalizes input/candidate, and persists expected_revision=None.
rows.bearing: The CLI must construct Candidate and acknowledge only the returned proposal-id string; any operation_revision input or ReviewRequired result would target a nonexistent API contract.

rows.locus: system.py `System.propose`: signature and why the core CLI must reach no source
rows.finding: propose(partition, operation, input_value) requires the configured candidate_source, invokes source.propose, canonicalizes its Candidate, and returns a proposal-id string.
rows.bearing: Core proposal submit must call submit_proposal, never propose; the latter is precisely the adapter/source reach that M3.5a must avoid extending.

rows.locus: models.py `Candidate`: field set, provenance mapping contract, canonicalization site
rows.finding: Candidate has only output and Mapping[str, object] provenance; _canonical_candidate requires the exact Candidate type, canonicalizes output, and canonicalizes dict(provenance) at 65,536 bytes.
rows.bearing: Submission input remains a separate library argument; the CLI should build Candidate(output, provenance), reject non-mapping provenance, and supply no revision field.

rows.locus: models.py `FunctionResolution`: field set and the `match is None` domain qualifier
rows.finding: FunctionResolution carries verification and optional match; System.resolve produces match=None exactly for failed verification, while a verified miss is FunctionMatch(matched=False). Hand-built values have no enforcing invariant.
rows.bearing: The CLI must branch on verification.passed before match, preserving failed-verdict versus verified-miss payloads instead of collapsing both through a nullable match.

rows.locus: function.py `FunctionVerification`: field set incl. the document that must not ship
rows.finding: FunctionVerification fields are passed, entries, document, function_hash, and ordered checks; a diagnostic hash can survive failure, while document is optional and may contain the full function.
rows.bearing: Resolve should expose verified, diagnostic function_hash, and projected checks, but never document; match/output fields belong only to a passing verification.

rows.locus: function.py `FunctionMatch` and `FunctionCheck`: field sets reaching a resolve payload
rows.finding: FunctionMatch fields are matched, output, and artifact_hash; FunctionCheck fields are key, passed, and detail, and verification stores checks as an ordered tuple.
rows.bearing: Passing resolve payloads can project match fields directly, while failed-verification payloads need ordered key/passed/detail objects and no match/output fields.

rows.locus: argparse abbreviation on `_parser()`: whether a prefix of a flag or leaf still parses
rows.finding: Live _parser() probes accepted root --part as --partition and nested function eval --bun/--in as --bundle/--input, but rejected abbreviated leaves function ev and proposal sho.
rows.bearing: M3.5a must disable option abbreviation on every parser node, not only the root, or removed/full-spelling flag predicates remain weaker than the grammar actually accepts.

rows.locus: tests/test_cli.py: how the leaf census is derived from `_parser()` and what it asserts
rows.finding: Recursive _SubParsersAction.choices traversal of _parser() yields 28 terminal leaves and 35 total parser nodes. test_cli.py has no full census: options() traverses only a requested path and asserts function eval’s three actions, requiredness, and help text.
rows.bearing: Adding resolve and proposal submit without removals should produce 30 leaves and 37 nodes; acceptance needs a recursive path census rather than extending the current one-leaf assertion.

rows.locus: System construction against an absent ledger path: does it create the file, and when
rows.finding: A live absent-path probe observed exists=False before System(path), then exists=True, size=208896 bytes, and user_version=2 immediately after the constructor returned.
rows.bearing: Resolve cannot construct ordinary System before proving the ledger path exists; otherwise the required missing-ledger read-only failure creates a fresh database as a side effect.

rows.locus: tests/test_cli.py shared fixture helpers: names, line anchors, caller counts
rows.finding: AST direct self-call census, shown as distinct caller methods/call sites: run_cli@170=147/270, payload@192=60/107, error@197=65/96, register@201=35/47, confirm@217=7/9, handle_once@247=4/5, promote_set@282=5/5, promoted_operation@299=43/46, compile_drafts@307=13/13, corrupt_middle_draft@315=5/5, report_and_failure_event_counts@346=2/4, receipt_history@368=12/13, live_document@2948=12/12, confirm_text@2954=2/2, corrupt_receipt_membership@2982=3/3, export_root@3433=22/22, temps@3436=11/13, run_offline@3968=29/40, exported_bundle@3978=32/32, resealed@3987=3/3, written@3996=8/11, eval_error@4001=12/15; unittest calls setUp directly.
rows.bearing: New tests should reuse the high-fanout harness and promoted-operation fixtures while adding direct submission setup; M3.5a removes nothing, so source-backed confirm/handle_once callers stay intact in this unit.

rows.locus: exit-6 census across shipped leaves: which object, which channel, which payload shape
rows.finding: Exactly four shipped leaves can exit 6: function eval sends stdout {artifact_hash,function_hash,matched,output}; verify-drafts sends stdout dataclass {passed,operation_revision,entries,skipped}; verify sends stdout {passed,entries,function_hash,checks}; export raises _Unverified and sends stderr {error,message,checks}. The first three return _Outcome; main emits that payload to stdout, while its _Unverified handler explicitly selects stderr.
rows.bearing: Resolve miss and failed-verification values should follow the stdout _Outcome precedents, not export’s exceptional stderr channel; their distinct key sets must remain explicit.

rows.locus: README.md + docs/: every sentence naming CLI submission or resolution grammar
rows.finding: Exhaustive census of README.md plus docs/adapter-protocol.md, docs/architecture.md, and docs/threat-model.md found 0 literal proposal-submit CLI grammars, 0 System.resolve mentions, and 0 backticked/root resolve commands. submit_proposal occurs 7 times (README 5, architecture 1, threat model 1) only as API prose; function eval occurs 5 times and legacy `handle` 11 times across those files.
rows.bearing: M3.5a must add operator-facing grammar and examples for both new channels; there is no existing resolve/submit CLI text to refresh, while legacy text remains because this unit removes nothing.

rows.locus: cli.py `proposal review` leaf: `--output` JSON handling and its stdin interaction
rows.finding: proposal review declares optional --output; when present, including -, dispatch parses it with _input and passes corrected_output, while omission leaves that keyword absent for System.review to validate against the decision.
rows.bearing: The shipped stdin precedent consumes the one process stdin through a single JSON option; proposal submit must pin whether its channel is aggregate or forbid competing - reads.

rows.locus: cli.py `_source` + `CommandCandidateSource` import: the reach M3.5a must not extend
rows.finding: cli.py imports CommandCandidateSource at module load; only handle calls _source, and every command then constructs System with source=None except handle’s concrete source.
rows.bearing: New resolve and proposal-submit dispatch must never call _source or expose source flags. Import removal cannot be an M3.5a predicate because handle remains until M3.5b.

rows.locus: json_value `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` / `parse_json`: bytes-vs-chars bound and its messages
rows.finding: DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES is 1,048,576. parse_json always enforces UTF-8 byte length and says JSON source exceeds N bytes; _input binary stdin says JSON stdin exceeds N bytes, while its text-host precheck counts characters and says characters before parse_json rechecks bytes.
rows.bearing: A multi-field submission envelope cannot reuse _input for any aggregate bound above 1 MiB; its reader must separately pin binary bytes, text-host behavior, and exact failure messages.

rows.locus: System.events + proposal.created event payload produced by a direct submission
rows.finding: A live direct-submission probe returned a str proposal ID and exactly one proposal.created event. System.events projected created_at_us, kind, payload, sequence, subject_id, and subject_type; subject_id equaled that proposal ID and payload was exactly {}, exposing no request, input, output, or provenance.
rows.bearing: proposal submit should acknowledge the returned proposal identity without candidate bytes or request identity; event assertions can prove the direct path wrote exactly one request-free public audit event.

rows.locus: roadmap submission-channel decision remains an explicit four-way open fork
rows.finding: The current roadmap deliberately leaves proposal-submit channel shape unruled and requires a spike comparing aggregate envelope, direct flags, stdin, and file with framing/error behavior.
rows.bearing: MAIN’s acceptance contract must select one channel after measuring all four; inheriting the draft’s --submission envelope would silently close an owner-recorded fork.

rows.locus: public System construction has no existing-only/read-only entry point
rows.finding: System.__init__ always builds Store; Store.__init__ uses O_CREAT|O_EXCL for an absent path and then _initialize opens a writable connection, begins IMMEDIATE, validates, and commits even for an existing ledger. Only later transactions can use private mode=ro.
rows.bearing: A true end-to-end existing-only/read-only resolve needs a new public construction mode outside cli.py; a path precheck only narrows the claim, remains race-prone, and still initializes existing files through a writer.

rows.locus: plan-draft submission envelope carries a field absent from the landed API
rows.finding: The draft fixes a four-key envelope containing operation_revision, but submit_proposal accepts no revision and always persists expected_revision=None under the current write lock.
rows.bearing: Any selected structured channel must omit operation_revision and delete the draft’s revision validation/max-edge probes; retaining it creates CLI-only semantics the library cannot consume.

rows.locus: plan-draft ReviewRequired acknowledgement is both wrong-type and request-bearing
rows.finding: ReviewRequired currently contains request_id, proposal_id, and status, while submit_proposal returns an exact str proposal ID and constructs no ReviewRequired value.
rows.bearing: The draft phrase request-free ReviewRequired is doubly false at HEAD; M3.5a must contract an ID acknowledgement instead of serializing or reshaping this lifecycle model.

rows.locus: legacy CLI removal and CommandCandidateSource import absence belong to M3.5b
rows.finding: The split roadmap assigns handle/request/source grammar, imports, fixtures, help, and operator-prose removal to M3.5b; all are present at the M3.5a base.
rows.bearing: M3.5a acceptance must assert preservation plus no new source reach, not legacy argparse failure or zero CommandCandidateSource imports; those draft predicates are deferred.

rows.locus: current missing-ledger CLI test bypasses the constructor that creates files
rows.finding: The shipped missing-ledger CLI test unlinks after constructing System and patches cli.System to return that instance. A real-main probe on an absent path instead returned 0 with [] and created a 208896-byte v2 ledger.
rows.bearing: Resolve’s missing-ledger acceptance must run unpatched main and assert directory/sidecar stability; reusing this test pattern would certify the private read transaction while missing the public constructor defect.

rows.locus: bare proposal-id return serialization at the main output seam
rows.finding: main sends any non-_Outcome result through _emit at status 0. A live _emit probe on prop_probe produced the exact bytes "prop_probe" followed by one newline, as a JSON string rather than an object.
rows.bearing: Returning submit_proposal directly gives a one-value JSON-string acknowledgement with no candidate bytes; wrapping it as {proposal_id:...} is a separate contract decision that tests must pin explicitly.

rows.locus: three-field aggregate envelope must lift byte, depth, and item limits
rows.finding: Library limits are input=1,048,576 bytes, output=1,048,576 bytes, provenance=65,536 bytes, depth=64 each, and 100,000 items each. Canonical {input,output,provenance} framing is 34 bytes, yielding aggregate maxima 2,162,722 bytes, depth 65, and 300,003 items.
rows.bearing: If MAIN selects an aggregate envelope, its outer parser must admit all three derived aggregate maxima before revalidating each field at library limits; default parse_json would reject valid combined maxima early.

rows.locus: strict JSON errors precede any envelope exact-key validator
rows.finding: parse_json rejects duplicate object keys during object_pairs construction, rejects non-finite and decimal/exponent numbers, and only then returns a canonical detached JSON value.
rows.bearing: A structured submission channel should parse strictly before checking type/key set, so duplicate required keys never collapse by last-wins and retain the existing ValidationError taxonomy.

rows.locus: argparse repeated-option behavior is last occurrence wins
rows.finding: The shipped function-eval test repeats bundle, input, and expected-hash options with invalid first values and valid last values; status 0 proves argparse forwards only each final occurrence and never grades earlier ones.
rows.bearing: M3.5a’s repeated-flag probes must choose and pin last-wins or add explicit duplicate rejection; parser defaults alone silently select last-wins for every new option.

rows.locus: direct-submission validation precedence and pre-transaction purity
rows.finding: The landed battery pins submit_proposal validation as partition, operation, input canonicalization, then Candidate canonicalization. Adjacent invalid input+candidate reports the input error, and every argument-rejected case opens zero transactions.
rows.bearing: CLI parsing/key/type errors must finish before the library call; once called, acceptance should preserve this precedence and prove malformed input/candidate paths leave request, proposal, event, bytes, and sidecars unchanged.

rows.locus: input, output, and provenance carry unequal library byte bounds
rows.finding: The submission battery proves provenance canonical JSON is capped at 65,536 bytes with exact error canonical JSON exceeds 65536 bytes, while the same object passes as output under the 1,048,576-byte default; input uses that same default.
rows.bearing: Every selected channel must preserve per-field bounds after outer parsing and include adjacent max/max+1 cases for all three fields, not only the aggregate transport bound.

rows.locus: same-value direct submissions are independent writes
rows.finding: Two byte-identical submit_proposal calls return unequal proposal IDs and add exactly two requests, two proposals, and two events; no content or caller token deduplicates them.
rows.bearing: CLI acceptance must submit the same envelope twice and observe two distinct acknowledgements and pending records; retry advice must never imply idempotency.

rows.locus: registered zero-entry functions resolve as verified ordinary misses
rows.finding: For null, object, array, and string inputs, a registered operation with zero promoted entries returns verification.passed=True, entries=0, and a non-null FunctionMatch with matched=False, output=None, artifact_hash=None.
rows.bearing: Root resolve must classify an empty current set as the ordinary stdout exit-6 miss shape, not not-found, unverified, or integrity; supported operation revision also retires to this state.

rows.locus: expected-function-hash is owned only by existing nested function leaves
rows.finding: The parser exposes --expected-function-hash on exactly three function leaves: verify, promote, and eval. System.resolve can accept it, but the authoritative M3.5a root grammar names only OPERATION and --input.
rows.bearing: Unless MAIN deliberately widens scope, root resolve must pass the library default None and reject this option; a cross-leaf isolation test should prevent nested function flags from leaking onto the new root leaf.

rows.locus: resolver argument errors are exact, ordered, and ledger-free
rows.finding: The resolver battery pins exact ValidationError texts and order partition→operation→expected hash→input; adjacent-invalid pairs select the earlier field, and every rejected argument makes zero Store.transaction and verify_function calls.
rows.bearing: Root resolve must let _input and System.resolve preserve this taxonomy while mapping it to stderr/2; acceptance should pair invalid fields and spy the ledger boundary, not test errors one at a time only.

rows.locus: deleted-ledger resolver error is exact and noncreating
rows.finding: After a valid System is constructed and its ledger is deleted, resolve raises IntegrityError with exact message ledger file is missing or unreadable and leaves the path absent.
rows.bearing: The new CLI should map this supported library failure to stderr exit 5 unchanged; its harder initial-absence case must reach the same observation without ordinary System construction recreating the file.

rows.locus: supported resolver state changes split failed verdict from verified miss
rows.finding: Suspension, evidence revocation, and a valid-but-wrong expected hash return verification.passed=False with document/match None; supported operation revision retires old artifacts and instead returns a passing zero-entry verified miss.
rows.bearing: The CLI matrix must classify state by the returned verification, not by change type: suspension/revocation use the failed-verdict payload, while a revised empty operation uses the ordinary miss payload.

rows.locus: resolve invokes no source and owns one read-only snapshot
rows.finding: The landed B18-B25 battery proves hit, miss, and failed resolve paths change no ledger bytes/dump/events, read no clock, allocate no ID, invoke no CandidateSource, and open exactly one Store.transaction(write=False); rejected arguments open zero.
rows.bearing: CLI integration should spy System.resolve once and source zero times, then compare bytes/events and transaction mode across all three states; routing through handle/propose or a second verification pass must fail.

rows.locus: root help still leads with fallback and the pre-addition command tree
rows.finding: Live parser introspection found 13 root choices, proposal children show/list/review, and the description Supervised LLM fallback that compiles confirmed behavior into exact deterministic artifacts.
rows.bearing: M3.5a adds one root choice and one proposal child without deleting old nodes; root/group/leaf help must describe deterministic resolution plus explicit capture while remaining truthful about still-present fallback until M3.5b.

rows.locus: cli module lacks the Candidate import required by direct submission
rows.finding: cli.py currently imports only CompilePolicy from models; no Candidate token occurs in the module, and no existing dispatch constructs a caller-supplied Candidate.
rows.bearing: M3.5a must add a direct models.Candidate dependency and construct Candidate(output=..., provenance=...) explicitly; routing through System.propose to avoid that import would violate source isolation.

rows.locus: direct submission ignores even a configured failing candidate source
rows.finding: The landed P03 battery configures a source whose propose would raise, calls submit_proposal successfully, and observes zero source calls; this separates direct submission from System.propose by live behavior.
rows.bearing: CLI submit acceptance should patch CandidateSource.propose to fail and still succeed with zero calls, proving the new leaf reaches submit_proposal rather than a source-backed convenience path.

rows.locus: direct-submission success footprint includes one private request row
rows.finding: A successful direct call adds exactly one request, one proposal, and one proposal.created event. The request stays pending and internally binds the proposal, but neither the returned ID nor event payload exposes its request ID.
rows.bearing: M3.5a must not claim storage is request-free; it should contract only a request-free public acknowledgement/event while pinning the current three-row footprint until M3.6 deletes private plumbing.

rows.locus: post-commit submission failure is ambiguous and forbids blind retry
rows.finding: submit_proposal documents zero writes before commit, but if commit succeeds and then fails it raises with no identifier while all three rows remain durable; recovery is pending-proposal listing, never retry.
rows.bearing: CLI help/error guidance must preserve commit ambiguity and non-idempotency. A StateError/exit-4 observation cannot certify absence, so tests must not promise all raised calls leave no proposal.

rows.locus: nested-leaf options remain isolated despite shared spellings
rows.finding: The shipped parser tests prove required/optional options on sibling function leaves do not leak: an option valid on one leaf is an unrecognized-arguments usage error on another.
rows.bearing: proposal submit and proposal review may both name output-like JSON, but each leaf must own only its selected options; resolve must likewise reject proposal/function-only flags in cross-leaf probes.

rows.locus: existing file-channel reader is bundle-specific and security-hardened
rows.finding: The only CLI file-value reader opens O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK, checks the descriptor is regular, bounds fstat plus max+1 read, decodes strict UTF-8, follows symlinks to regular files, and reports function-bundle-specific errors at a 64-MiB limit.
rows.bearing: If MAIN selects a submission file channel, it must genericize these descriptor guarantees and use submission bounds/messages; treating a path as ordinary text or reusing the helper unchanged would misstate both security and limits.

rows.locus: two JSON options cannot independently consume one stdin stream
rows.finding: Live probes on text and binary stdin called _input(-) twice: the first returned the sole JSON value, and the second raised invalid JSON: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) because the first read consumed the stream.
rows.bearing: A direct-flags channel must reject multiple - values before reading or define one aggregate stdin owner; sequential _input calls create option-order-dependent failures rather than three independent channels.

rows.locus: both new stateful leaves inherit db and partition gates before System construction
rows.finding: _run requires db then partition for every command except function eval, with exact parser errors --db or CEMENT_DB is required and --partition or CEMENT_PARTITION is required, before it constructs System.
rows.bearing: Root resolve is ledger-backed and proposal submit writes state, so both must remain after these ordered gates; only their JSON parsing order relative to the gates is a contract choice that tests must pin.

rows.locus: all argparse failures become one machine-readable usage class
rows.finding: Every parser node uses _JSONArgumentParser.error to raise _UsageError; main emits {error:invalid,message:<argparse text>} on stderr and returns 2 instead of argparse usage text or SystemExit.
rows.bearing: New required arguments, unknown options, invalid choices, abbreviations, and cross-leaf leakage must be asserted through exact JSON stderr/status, not parse_args exceptions alone.

rows.locus: resolve payload vocabulary is a custom CLI projection, not any model shape
rows.finding: The proposed success keys use verified while FunctionVerification names passed; FunctionResolution nests verification/match, and no model directly has verified, function_hash, matched, artifact_hash, output as one field set. The failed draft shape also omits entries, document, match, and output.
rows.bearing: Implementation must build two explicit dictionaries and tests must freeze exact key sets on hit, miss, and failed verification; dataclass/asdict serialization cannot satisfy the stated vocabulary safely.
